q.t: A picture is symmetrical when:
o: you can fold it so one half lies exactly on the other half
q.e: Symmetrical means the two halves match exactly when folded on the line.

q.t: Which capital letter is symmetrical when folded down the middle?
q.e: The left and right halves of A match. F, J and G look different on each side.

q.t: Which can cover a floor with no gaps and no overlaps?
q.e: Square sides fit flat against each other; round shapes always leave gaps between them.

q.t: A mala has beads in the order red, red, blue, blue, blue, blue, red, red. Is it symmetrical?
q.e: Read from either end it is red, red, blue, blue — both halves match.

q.t: Which of these is symmetrical?
q.e: A butterfly’s left wing matches its right wing.

q.t: A painter draws half a symmetrical picture. A mirror is held on the fold line. What do you see?
q.e: The mirror shows the same half flipped, which is exactly the missing half.

q.t: You walk forward and then turn right two times. Which way are you facing now?
q.e: Two right turns make you turn all the way around to face the opposite way.

q.t: Which digit has a line down its middle so both halves match?
q.e: The left and right halves of 8 match; 2, 4 and 7 look different on each side.

q.t: If you try to tile a path with circles, what happens?
q.e: Round edges touch only at points, leaving gaps between them.

q.t: To make a cat mask, you fold paper, draw half a cat along the fold and cut it out. When you open it, the two eyes are:
o: the same size, one on each side
q.e: Cutting through the folded paper cuts both halves at once, so they match exactly.

q.t: Which word looks the same when you hold a mirror beside it?
q.e: M and O are symmetrical and MOM reads the same both ways, so its mirror image is MOM.

q.t: Which capital letter is NOT symmetrical?
q.e: A, H and T can be folded so the halves match; F cannot be folded that way at all.

q.t: In how many ways can you fold a square so that one half lies exactly on the other?
q.e: Fold edge to edge (2 ways: up-down and left-right) and corner to corner (2 ways): 4.

q.t: In how many ways can you fold a rectangle that is not a square so the halves match exactly?
q.e: Only edge to edge, up-down or left-right. Folding corner to corner does not match for a long rectangle.

q.t: R is a red bead and B is a blue bead. Which mala is symmetrical?
o: B R R R R R R B
R R R R R R B B
B B R R R R R R
R B R R R R R B
q.e: B R R R R R R B reads the same from both ends. The others change when you read them backwards.

q.t: In the mirror game, Soni puts a counter 2 boxes to the left of the mirror line. Where must Avi put his?
o: 2 boxes to the right of the line
2 boxes to the left of the line
4 boxes to the right of the line
q.e: A mirror image is the same distance from the line, but on the other side.

q.t: The painter can show half a picture and use a mirror for the rest. For which thing will this trick NOT work?
q.e: The mirror trick only works for symmetrical things. The letter R is not symmetrical.

q.t: Which shapes can cover a floor with no gaps?
q.e: Rectangles have straight sides and square corners, so they fit together tightly.

q.t: You stand facing the giant wheel. You make 3 square-corner turns to the right. Where is the giant wheel now?
q.e: After 2 right turns the wheel is behind you; one more right turn brings it round to your right side.

q.t: Which of these is NOT symmetrical?
q.e: Fold L any way and the halves don’t match. Kites, T and H can be folded to match.

q.t: A mala has 4 red (R) and 4 blue (B) beads. Which one is symmetrical?
o: R B B R R B B R
R R B B R R B B
R R R R B B B B
B R B R B R B R
q.e: R B B R R B B R reads the same from both ends; the others change when read backwards.

q.t: A symmetrical rangoli has 3 flowers in its left half. How many flowers are in the whole rangoli?
q.e: The right half matches the left half exactly: 3 + 3 = 6.

q.t: Which word looks the same in a mirror held beside it?
q.e: T and O are symmetrical and TOOT reads the same both ways. B, K, L, P, S and E are not symmetrical that way.

q.t: A path is 6 square tiles long and 2 tiles wide. How many tiles cover it?
A path needs 20 square tiles. Tiles come in packs of 4. How many packs are needed?
In how many ways can you fold the capital letter H so that its halves match?
q.e: Fold it left-to-right or top-to-bottom; both times the halves match.

q.t: From the entry, the chaupal is 3 steps forward and then 2 steps to the right. To get back without turning around, you go 2 steps ___ and then 3 steps back.
q.e: To undo a move, do the opposite: undo 2 steps right with 2 steps left.

q.t: Which capital letter is symmetrical?
q.e: W’s left and right halves match. N, S and Z have no fold line that matches.

q.t: Two equal triangles make one square tile. How many triangles make a path of 5 such squares?
q.e: Each square needs 2 triangles: 5 × 2 = 10.

q.t: Which can tile a floor with no gaps and no overlaps?
q.e: Equal triangles fit side to side (two make a square); circles always leave gaps.

q.t: A mala has 8 beads in a line: 6 blue and 2 red. It must be symmetrical. Where can the 2 red beads go?
q.e: The mirror partner of bead 1 is bead 8 (both at the ends), so they must both be red.

q.t: How many different symmetrical 8-bead malas can be made with 6 blue and 2 red beads?
q.e: The two reds must be mirror partners: beads 1 and 8, 2 and 7, 3 and 6, or 4 and 5 — that is 4 ways.

q.t: A symmetrical rangoli has 7 petals in its left half and 1 big petal lying right on the fold line. How many petals in all?
q.e: Both halves have 7 (7 + 7 = 14), and the one on the line is counted once: 15.

q.t: A square courtyard is 4 tiles by 4 tiles. Only the tiles along the outside edge are coloured. How many tiles are coloured?
q.e: There are 4 × 4 = 16 tiles. The inside 2 × 2 = 4 are not on the edge: 16 − 4 = 12.

q.t: You walk on the blue lane, turn right onto the green lane, then turn left. Which way are you facing now, compared with the start?
o: the same way as at the start
q.e: A left turn undoes a right turn, so you face your starting direction again.

q.t: You make 4 square-corner turns to the left, one after another. Which way do you face now?
o: the same way as at the start
q.e: Two left turns face you backwards; two more turn you all the way round again.

q.t: Stalls stand in a row, numbered 1, 2, 3 … Soni is at stall 3. She walks 4 stalls to the right, then 2 stalls back to the left. Which stall is she at?
Which of these has exactly ONE fold line where the halves match?
q.e: A only folds left-to-right. H has 2 fold lines, a square has 4, and a circle has very many.

q.t: Each of Soni’s tiles is made of 1 square and 2 triangles. How many triangles does she need for 6 tiles?
q.e: 2 triangles per tile: 6 × 2 = 12.

q.t: You write a small letter ‘b’ and hold a mirror beside it. What does the mirror show?
q.e: A mirror beside the letter flips left and right, so the round part moves to the other side: d.
